name: QNAP
author: Netlens
description: Shows a QNAP NAS (QTS 5 or QuTS hero with Container Station 3) as a host with its Container Station containers as guests: state, image, compose project, the ports they publish, and the address of a container that has its own IP on your network. Reads through Container Station's web API, read-only. Needs an account in the administrators group (Container Station offers no read-only role).

info.title: Set up a user for Netlens on the QNAP
info.text: Container Station's web API only lets administrators in, so Netlens needs an account of its own in the administrators group. Keep it dedicated and small: in QTS open Control Panel > Privilege > Users > Create, name it netlens with a long random password, put it in the administrators group, and deny it every shared folder. Do not switch on 2-step verification for this account (a program cannot answer it). In Control Panel > Security > Security Level allow access only from the machine Netlens runs on. The address is the QTS web address: https://<NAS address>:443 (or http://<NAS address>:8080); leave 'Verify TLS certificate' off while the NAS uses its self-signed certificate. Netlens signs in for a few seconds at each sync and signs out again.
info.code:
# Control Panel > Privilege > Users > Create
#   Name: netlens   (a long, random password)
#   Groups: administrators, no shared folders
# Control Panel > Security > Security Level: allow only the Netlens machine
# In Netlens: address https://<NAS address>:443, user netlens, that password

config.label: QNAP systems
config.help: One line per QNAP: its address (the QTS web address, for example https://192.168.0.40:443) and the user name and password of the Netlens user.

config.label: Verify TLS certificate
config.help: Leave this off while the NAS uses its own self-signed certificate.
